I will release the code once I shake a few more bugs out of it. <@!259648573401071617> , I am correct in assuming that to use the jumpdest of fixed size splitting, the evm will need to keep a track of what code is used? > offset of the 128 byte chunk isn't needed, because it can be determined by virtue of where is sits in the trie? yeah exactly, trie key would be the offset of the first byte in the chunk > jumpdest of fixed size splitting, the evm will need to keep a track of what code is used? do you mean how can evm tell if a jumpdest in a fixed sized chunk is valid and not pushdata? > splitting code based on function id is coming together. so you're aiming to have each solidity function as one chunk? that might get easier with the subroutines eip. <@!425279588009246720> is thinking about that too > do you mean how can evm tell if a jumpdest in a fixed sized chunk is valid and not pushdata? <@!259648573401071617> I did a typo which made my question confusing. For the "split by jumpdest approach", or the "split code into fixed size chunks approach", am I correct in saying that the EVM will need to keep a track of what code is used? > so you're aiming to have each solidity function as one chunk? that might get easier with the subroutines eip. <@!425279588009246720> is thinking about that too <@!259648573401071617> Correct Having subroutines will help with next code, but won't help with contracts that have already been deployed.
